chapters.title: First Wings
chapters.subtitle: NAS Minneapolis, Aug–Oct 1943
chapters.text: On 17 August 1943 Thomas Edward Goss signed into naval aviation. His first logbook page records primary training in the N2S "Yellow Peril" biplane: 34.2 hours with an instructor and 59.5 solo, finished on 23 October 1943.
chapters.rank_basis: likely: Marine pilots trained as Navy cadets until they earned their wings

chapters.title: Pensacola
chapters.subtitle: NAS Pensacola, Nov 1943–Mar 1944
chapters.text: Intermediate training at the "Annapolis of the Air": instrument hops in the SNV Valiant, then formation and gunnery in the SNJ Texan. On 21 March 1944 he was rated an instrument pilot. Part of March is missing from the scanned pages.
chapters.rank_basis: likely: Marine pilots trained as Navy cadets until they earned their wings

chapters.title: Dive Bombers
chapters.subtitle: NAS Miami, Apr–May 1944
chapters.text: Operational training in the SBD-5 Dauntless with radioman-gunners in the rear seat: bombing runs, tactics, field carrier landing practice, and long navigation flights over the Florida Straits.
chapters.rank_basis: likely newly commissioned; the log does not record the date

chapters.title: Stateside
chapters.subtitle: VMSB-474 workups, Aug–Oct 1944
chapters.text: Now a Marine second lieutenant, he joined scout-bomber squadron VMSB-474: dive and glide bombing, strafing, radar and homing-beacon hops, oxygen flights, battle problems. The log never names the base, so these flights are counted but not placed on the map. Most of September is missing from the scan.
chapters.rank_basis: as he signed his logbook on 1 September 1944

chapters.title: The Solomons
chapters.subtitle: Green Island & Piva, Nov 1944
chapters.text: By late November 1944 he had joined VMSB-341, the "Torrid Turtles," flying the SBD-6 from Green Island and over to Piva on Bougainville. From here on his rear-seat gunner on every combat mission is Matson. December and January read "NO FLIGHTS": Marine Aircraft Group 24 was moving its squadrons by sea from the Solomons, by way of New Guinea and Leyte, to Lingayen Gulf on Luzon.
chapters.rank_basis: still a 2nd Lt or newly a 1st Lt; the log does not say

chapters.title: Luzon
chapters.subtitle: Battle of Manila, Feb 1945
chapters.text: Ten strikes in eleven days as the Battle of Manila raged: Rosario, Corregidor, Wawa, Fort McKinley, Marikina Field, Calamba. VMSB-341 flew from Mangaldan, a strip it helped build a few miles inland from Lingayen Gulf, not from a carrier; he would not qualify aboard a carrier until 1953. Its close support for the 1st Cavalry and 11th Airborne near Wawa-Lobac is his entry for 14 February.
chapters.rank_basis: still a 2nd Lt or newly a 1st Lt; the log does not say

chapters.title: Mindanao
chapters.subtitle: Zamboanga, Apr–Jul 1945
chapters.text: In late March VMSB-341 moved south to Moret Field at Zamboanga. From there he flew strikes on Jolo, Malabang, Davao and the Bukidnon highlands, sometimes landing at Malabang to refuel before the run home. On his final combat page he totaled it himself: 31 completed strikes, 6 incomplete.
chapters.rank_basis: still a 2nd Lt or newly a 1st Lt; the log does not say

chapters.title: Home
chapters.subtitle: VMSB-932, Oct–Nov 1945
chapters.text: Back in North Carolina with VMSB-932, flying the SB2C Helldiver in the war's last weeks of peacetime flying: dive bombing practice, division tactics and parade rehearsals over Cherry Point.
chapters.rank_basis: still a 2nd Lt or newly a 1st Lt; the log does not say

chapters.title: Recalled
chapters.subtitle: Cherry Point, 1951–52
chapters.text: Six years later the Korean War brought him back. Refresher flying in the SNJ, then the F4U-4 Corsair, and twin-engine SNB instrument training at MCAS Cherry Point. Two cross-country trips went home to family in Wisconsin, including one over Christmas 1951.
chapters.rank_basis: rank not recorded in the log

chapters.title: Korea
chapters.subtitle: VMO-6, Sep–Nov 1952
chapters.text: With observation squadron VMO-6 he flew the OE-1 Bird Dog from strip A-9, spotting artillery (A/S) and directing air strikes (TAO) over the hills north of the line. His most frequent target was Taedŏk-san, a hill just north of Panmunjŏm, where the truce talks dragged on below him.
chapters.rank_basis: rank not recorded in the log

chapters.title: Skyraiders
chapters.subtitle: VMC-2, Jan–Jun 1953
chapters.text: Home again, flying AD Skyraiders with VMC-2: night flights, hunter-killer exercises, and on 13 April 1953 carrier qualification aboard USS Bennington off Guantánamo. The final entry, 24 June 1953 at Edenton, reads simply: "CRASH!"
chapters.rank_basis: rank not recorded in the log; he finished his service as a Captain
